quandoUsar: Frequently asked questions on a landing page where the open item should stand out from the block, with an icon before each question.
Lists where several answers can stay open at the same time, with `multiple`.
Accordions whose state comes from outside, such as the URL or a form, with `value` and `onValueChange`.
quandoEvitar: Use `accordion` on dense pages or documentation, where thin dividers and less motion fit better.
Use `collapsible` for a single region that opens and closes.
Use `faq-section` when you need the whole question section, with topics or search.

teclado.acao: Opens or closes the focused item; without `multiple`, opening one closes the others.
Moves focus to the next or previous title, skipping disabled ones and wrapping to the first after the last.
Moves focus to the first or last enabled title.

acessibilidade: Each title is a `<button>` inside a heading of level `headingLevel` (default 3), with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `region` tied to the title.
When it finishes closing, the panel gets `visibility: hidden` and leaves the Tab order and the accessibility tree; the icon and plus sign are hidden from the screen reader.
Items with `disabled` use the button's native `disabled` and are skipped by the arrows.
movimento: The open item breaks away from its neighbors: the margins grow from 3 px up to `gap` and the corners facing the space round up to `radius`, on a spring with a small bounce.
The height opens with the same bounce and closes on a no-overshoot spring; the content moves down 10 px as it appears and the plus sign rotates 135° until it becomes an x.
With “reduce motion” on, margins, corners, height, and icon change instantly, and the button's grow on hover is turned off.
notasIA: `value` is always a list of strings, even without `multiple`, and `onValueChange` receives the whole list; all start closed (`defaultValue` is `[]`).
When turning off `multiple` with controlled state, trim the list yourself, as the demo does with `current.slice(-1)`; the component does not do this.
Each item needs a unique `value`; `title` accepts any React node and `icon` is optional. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/bouncy-accordion/bouncy-accordion`.
